newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S.Korean tender win should help prices - AMLC.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S.Korean tender win should help prices - AMLC.

text.p: Australia's successful performance in the latest South Korean grassfed beef tender should help improve beef prices in Australia, Wendy Leeds, beef marketing co-ordinator for the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp (AMLC), told Reuters.

The latest tender, which Australia dominated in the grassfed section, was Korea's largest in the fullset section in the 1996 quota year and second-largest in the grassfed quarter beef section, Leeds said.
"Australia did extremely well, picking up practically all of the fullset award," she said.
Details of the award were announced on Monday.
Reduced competition from New Zealand reflected that country's seasonal supply situation, AMLC said.
Not all of the tender offer was awarded in the latest round, with 468 tonnes of grassfed fullsets required to go to re-tender on September 17, AMLC said.

Prices for grassfed fullsets in the latest tender rose by an average of 28 cents per kg on an Australian currency free alongside basis (involving the U.S. cost and freight price converted to Australian currency with freight costs deducted), compared with the previous tender held on August 16.
Prices for grassfed quarter beef also improved in the latest tender, AMLC said.
Australia dominated grassfed fullsets in the latest tender, securing 97.2 percent, or 1,260 tonnes, with New Zealand taking the remaining 2.8 percent, or 36 tonnes.
Australian exporters also received 86.8 percent, or 4,350 tonnes, of the grassfed quarter beef tender, with New Zealand securing 13.2 percent, or 660 tonnes.

The Korean government agency the Livestock Products Marketing Organisation (LPMO) had now purchased 87,732 tonnes boneless equivalent of its minimum quota commitment of 88,200 tonnes for 1996, AMLC said.
With the re-tender of 468 tonnes of grassfed fullsets, this would fulfil LPMO's minimum purchase quota for this year, it said.
